items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1976-02-13
items.q: I'll never forget the time I went to work with Johnny Detroit... I went to work with him at Suburban Gardens

ctx.x: Well, it's been pointed out, I think, in that book that just came out on Biggs, that a lot of solo passages he managed to create. And they only could have been created by someone who played by ear. Sure. Because he went off on a note, for instance, that a person who read, a well-trained red musician, would have thought it was a mistake and completely stopped the solo. Yeah. But Biggs managed to go on because he didn't have that reading novel. So it actually worked to his best.

And this is true of many of the people who have studied music. Like, I have people come up right now and tell me, you know, I'm playing something. And they say, how long did you study? I say, oh, I actually studied about six months. I said, six months? I studied ten years. I can't play anything, you know? They said, all I can do is when I got the notes there, you know, I can play it. But when they take the music away from me, I can't play it. Well, that's what the old musicians in New Orleans used to avoid. They…

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: I had a chance to go to work at Old Suburban Gardens in 1931 or 1932... Johnny Detroit had the band out there... I had the chance to take his place... Johnny Detroit came around... Johnny Detroit says, well he said, you know something? He says, I got to give you credit kid.

ctx.x: So many of them, you learn new names every day. Yeah, that's just it.

There were many names. But as you said before, Dick, I think that's a good thing to think about. While we're talking about these fellows, I don't know if you would say that they were all real jazz piano players. That is, in a real jazz sense. They may have been able to play with dance bands and play, but I think that they were more or less, most of some of these names that we mentioned, they were legitimate musicians. They played more or less by music, strictly. I don't know if they even played, if they were even…
What about Louis Armstrong? Did you hear him when he was at the Samaritan Gardens?
